To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

24-hours blood pressures and self recorded blood pressure are more sensitive techniques than cuff blood pressures to recognize patients with hypertension. 24-hours blood pressure and self recorded blood presure are more adequate techniques for the judgement of hypertension than cuff blood pressures.

the 24-hours-blood-pressure determination is more sensitive than the conventional blood pressure measurements and that self recording blood pressures are as sensitive as the conventional measurements.
the 24-hour blood pressures are a good indicator for the real blood pressure of the hypertensive patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the self-recorded blood pressure (SRBP) and 24-hours-blood-pressure (24h-BP) readings are more sensitive techniques than the conventional cuff blood pressure (CBP) readings.
the evaluation of the value of indirect 24-hours-blood-pressure-determinations and of blood-pressure-self-control for the diagnosis and treatment of arterial hypertension.

the question whether the 24-hours blood pressure readings and blood pressure self-recordings are more sensitive than the cuff blood pressure readings for the detection of hypertension and the evaluation of the blood pressure lowering effects of drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 24-hours-blood-pressure readings and the self-recorded blood pressure readings are new, more sensible techniques for the judgement of hypertension.
the 24 hours ambulatory blood pressure monitoring and the blood pressure self-control are the most important new tools for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of hypertension.
the new methods of blood pressure determination are more accurate than the traditional method and therefore more reliable for the judgement of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosis of hypertension has to be made with 24-hours blood pressure recordings or self-recorded blood pressures.
we should not treat our patients with hypertension only with the help of the cuff blood pressure.
we should treat the patients with hypertension as early as possible with the lowest dose of antihypertensives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new methods of blood pressure measurement and self control are very helpful for diagnosis and treatment of hypertension.
we can use 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) to detect white coat hypertension.
the new methods are very sensitive and help us to diagnose and treat patients more accurately.
